# Media rights manifest

**Every asset in this repository is original work created for this project, or is generated by
its own code. No third-party film, script, subtitle file, recording, image, font, icon set,
dataset or model weight is used anywhere.**

That claim is unusual for a media project, so this document states exactly what exists, who
created it, and under what terms — asset by asset.

---

## 1. The demonstration programme — *The Lumière Protocol*

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | Original short dramatic work: dialogue, scene descriptions, translations |
| **Created for** | AccessPulse, for the Agentic Cinema contest |
| **Author** | The AccessPulse project |
| **Licence** | Apache-2.0 — the same licence as the code |
| **Location** | `src/accesspulse/media.py` |
| **Third-party content** | **None** |

**What it consists of:**

- 12 timed dialogue lines across 3 scenes, 3 characters (ELIAS, NOOR, ARCHIVIST), 85-second loop
- Complete translations into French, German and Spanish — human-written parallel text, not
  machine translation, and not sourced from any existing subtitle file
- 5 scene descriptions authored for audio description, placed in the dialogue gaps
- A declared French sign-language (LSF) interpreter feed, represented as frame statistics

**Why the title.** *The Lumière Protocol* is a newly-coined title for this work. "Lumière" is a
common noun in French ("light") and the surname of the cinema pioneers, who died in 1948 and
1954; the name is used here only as an allusion in an original title, and no Lumière film,
footage, still or trademark is used, referenced or reproduced.

**Themes.** Three archivists in a projection booth argue about a reel that has been missing
since 1962. The material is deliberately mundane: no real people, no real organisations, no
personal data, nothing distressing, nothing that could be mistaken for a real work.

**No encoded media.** The programme is modelled as a timed event list, not as a video or audio
file. There is no encoded picture, no recorded audio, no recorded signing, no rendered subtitle
file. Nothing was captured from a camera or a microphone, so there are no performers, no
performer rights and no releases to obtain.

## 2. Everything else in the repository

| Asset | Origin | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| All source code (`src/`, `bench/`, `tools/`, `tests/`) | Written for this project | Apache-2.0 |
| Grafana dashboards and alert rules (`observability/grafana/`) | **Generated** from the SLO definitions by `tools/generate_grafana_assets.py` | Apache-2.0 |
| Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope configuration | Written for this project | Apache-2.0 |
| The web UI (`src/accesspulse/web/`) | Written for this project — no framework, no component library, no CSS toolkit, no bundler | Apache-2.0 |
| Fonts | **None bundled.** The UI uses the reader's system font stack (`-apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif`) | n/a |
| Icons and imagery | **None.** The only glyphs are Unicode characters (`◎ ✓ ✕ ! · ▶`) rendered by the reader's own fonts | n/a |
| Favicon | An inline SVG data-URI containing one Unicode character, written in the HTML | Apache-2.0 |
| Colour palette | Chosen for this project against WCAG contrast requirements ([ACCESSIBILITY_CONFORMANCE.md](ACCESSIBILITY_CONFORMANCE.md)) | Apache-2.0 |
| Fault library | Written for this project | Apache-2.0 |
| Benchmark and calibration results | Generated by running this repository's own code | Apache-2.0 |
| Documentation | Written for this project | Apache-2.0 |

**No CDN, no remote asset.** The product loads nothing from a third-party host at runtime: no
script, stylesheet, font, image or telemetry beacon. Everything the browser receives is served
by the application itself.

---

## 3. Third-party software

The repository *depends on* open-source software, which is a different thing from containing
third-party content. Every dependency is a permissively-licensed library obtained from PyPI at
install time and none is vendored into this repository. The full list, with versions and
licences, is the software bill of materials: [`sbom.json`](../sbom.json) (CycloneDX), regenerated
by `python tools/generate_sbom.py`.

Runtime services used in the full-stack configuration — Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo,
Pyroscope, and the official Grafana MCP server — run as their own upstream container images
under their own licences (AGPL-3.0 for Grafana, Apache-2.0 for Prometheus, Loki and Tempo).
They are pulled by `docker compose`; nothing from them is redistributed here.

---

## 4. Model weights

**None are bundled and none are downloaded.** The text models in `probes/text.py` — a character
n-gram language identifier and a hashed n-gram embedding — are *fitted at runtime from the
programme corpus in this repository*, in a few milliseconds, with no pretrained weights
involved. The optional Gemini reasoning plane is an API call to Vertex AI; no weights are
distributed.

---

Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Google Cloud, Gemini and Vertex AI are trademarks

## 6. How the claim is enforced

`MEDIA_MANIFEST` in `src/accesspulse/media.py` declares the provenance in machine-readable form:

```python
{
  "title": "The Lumiere Protocol",
  "origin": "original work created for AccessPulse",
  "licence": "Apache-2.0 (same as repository)",
  "third_party_content": "none",
  ...
}
```

`test_demonstration_media_is_original` asserts it on every CI run. Any future contribution that
introduced third-party media would have to falsify that manifest to get past the test.

---

## 7. Contributions

Contributions are accepted under Apache-2.0, and a contribution that adds media must be original
work by the contributor or content the contributor holds the rights to relicense. There is no
route in this repository for adding third-party film, subtitle or audio assets.
